title: How This Journal Works
excerpt: A tour of the journal's layouts and content blocks, written as an article that uses them all.
author: Mono Chromattic
imageCaption: Every layout here is driven by plain JSON and Markdown.
content:
## One article, many layouts

Each entry in `assets/data/journal/index.json` picks a **layout** with its `template` field: `cinematic`, `editorial`, `magazine` or `photo-essay`. The article body is ordinary **Markdown**, so you get headings, lists, quotes, tables and `code` for free.

### Markdown features

- Bold, *italic* and [links](https://commonmark.org/help/)
- Numbered and bulleted lists
- Tables and block quotes

> Write the story in Markdown, then add blocks for the pictures.

### Content blocks

Blocks follow the Markdown in every layout. This article uses most of them: a paragraph with an image, an image list, a gallery and a quote.

blocks.caption: paragraph-image, aligned left.
blocks.text:
A `paragraph-image` block places text beside a photo. Set `align` to `left` or `right`.

Images can point at a Gallery photo with `collection` and `src`, so the title and alt text are reused automatically.
Layouts change how a story feels. The story stays the same.
